beats.name: Spencer Silver
beats.role: 3M scientist. He tried to make a super strong adhesive and made a weak, reusable one instead.

beats.lead: For five years, nobody wanted it
beats.text: Silver promoted the adhesive inside 3M as a solution without a problem and found no supporters.
beats.note: It had been aimed at the aerospace industry.

beats.name: Art Fry
beats.role: Heard Silver's seminar, then used the adhesive to hold a bookmark in his hymn book.

beats.text: In 1977 3M test marketed it as "Press 'n Peel" in four cities, and the results were disappointing.
beats.note: In 1978 free samples went to offices in Boise, Idaho, and over 90 per cent of recipients said they would buy it.

beats.text: The yellow was chance. It matched the scrap paper in the next lab.

beats.line: A failed glue found its job in a hymn book.
